problems.statement: Three Line 3-only changes (Corvane bar from 3 Aug, spindle service deferred on 6 Aug and 3 Sep, 12-hour pattern from 10 Aug) landed within days of each other, so the yield loss cannot yet be attributed to one of them, and nobody owns the combined effect.

Deferred quarterly spindle service has let spindle wear grow (runout 2-3 um to 4-11 um, with L3-02 and L3-05 above the 5 um limit and L3-02 vibration up 1.9 to 4.1 mm/s), which is a real and material contributor to journal-size scatter and chatter.

Corvane bar, whose within-lot hardness scatter widened after its Sept billet-source change even though all readings stay in spec, increases tool deflection and size scatter and is a live cause of the decline.

The worn-spindle and wide-hardness-scatter effects interact and compound (a worn bearing plus variable cutting load), which could explain why all six machines worsened and the tight-tolerance long-shaft machines worsened most.
Twelve-hour-shift fatigue directly causes the yield loss, as the Plant Manager presents; the evidence counts against this as the primary cause.
The nine new, under-trained operators are the cause of the decline.

Inspection or measurement drift (CMM, gauge R&R, program, reject criteria) creates an apparent FPY drop; the metrology records are stable and the Halvard receiving rejects independently confirm a real defect increase.
Manual wear-offset keying errors from more frequent insert changes add to size scatter, but this is a secondary mechanism downstream of chatter and cannot be separated with current defect codes.

causalClaims.to: Deferral of spindle service (no maintenance window)

causalClaims.from: Spindle service deferral and extra machine-hours

causalClaims.to: Higher reject rate (6.1% to 9.8% by lot)

causalClaims.from: Switch from Tamsworth to Corvane bar (7.5% saving)

actions.action: Pull the CMM results for the roughly 1,400 long shafts overflowed to Line 6 (Corvane bar, serviced spindle, 8-hour shifts) and compare them with L3-02 and L3-05 over the same period.
actions.rationale: This is the cheapest available natural experiment separating steel from spindle wear and shift pattern, using data that already exists.

actions.action: Do the overdue spindle service on all six Line 3 lathes now, two at a time on weekend shifts, starting with L3-02 and L3-05, logging before and after runout, vibration and per-machine rejects.
actions.rationale: Runout is out of limit on two machines, the service is cheap, reversible and now affordable with a 1.2-week backlog, and the staggered before-and-after data also tests the spindle hypothesis.

actions.action: Order the two Tamsworth trial lots and run a deliberate comparison (Tamsworth on serviced and unserviced machines, Corvane on serviced machines) before deciding on steel.
actions.rationale: The 3% premium is small against about $6,700 a week of excess scrap, and the trial breaks the steel and spindle confounding that history cannot.

actions.action: Send Halvard the containment plan (keep 100% CMM, add a journal-diameter check and sort suspect inventory) and describe root cause as under investigation.
actions.rationale: Rejects at Halvard are rising (35 to 290 PPM) and the 13 Nov plan is due, but the cause is not verified, so containment is right and a root-cause claim is not.

actions.action: Link each CMM reject to machine, bar lot, operator login and time via the lathe cycle-counter logs (kept for 180 days) and the MES, and start recording this going forward.
actions.rationale: This enables time-in-shift, per-machine and per-lot analysis that is currently impossible and would otherwise be lost as the logs expire.

actions.action: Ask Corvane for billet-source change data and hardness-scatter capability, and add within-lot hardness SD as an incoming acceptance criterion.
actions.rationale: Scatter rose after the unannounced-until-September source change and is invisible to a pass/fail spec check.

actions.action: Return Line 3 to 8-hour shifts, but sequence it so it does not blur the service and steel comparisons, and do not present it as confirmed to be the fix.
actions.rationale: The backlog now ships at 8-hour capacity and fatigue is reported, but the evidence does not show shifts as the cause, so this is a reversible welfare and maintenance-window measure rather than a cure.

actions.action: Adopt the Corvane 7.5% saving (about $210,000 a year) as permanent now.
actions.rationale: If steel contributes, excess scrap (about $6,700 a week, roughly $350,000 a year) and customer escapes outweigh the saving, and the cause is unverified.

actions.action: Cut Line 3 final CMM inspection from 100% to 1-in-10 sampling.
actions.rationale: Customer rejects are already rising, sampling would let defects escape to Halvard, and it would remove the data needed to diagnose the problem.

actions.action: Blame or retrain the new operators, or lengthen training as the yield fix.
actions.rationale: New and experienced operators reject at the same rate, and FPY fell before any new operator ran alone.

actions.action: Introduce change control, so that supplier, maintenance-deferral and shift-pattern changes on one line are reviewed together with a yield and quality impact check.
actions.rationale: Three unreviewed concurrent changes made the diagnosis impossible and were decided by different functions in isolation.

nextEvidence: CMM results, by shaft and journal dimension, for the 1,400 long shafts run on Line 6 (Corvane bar, serviced spindle, 8-hour shifts) versus L3-02 and L3-05 in the same weeks.
Staggered spindle-service results on Line 3 (before and after runout, vibration and per-machine reject rate on the same Corvane lot) plus the Tamsworth trial-lot comparison.
Lathe cycle-counter and CMM serial matching to give reject rate by hour of shift, machine, bar lot and hardness reading for the last 180 days.
output.summary: The 12-hour shift is not shown to be the cause. The scrap-tag timing is a batch-writing artifact, and new and experienced operators reject at the same rate. Measurement drift is ruled out. Two unverified, confounded causes remain: Corvane bar, whose hardness scatter widened after a supplier billet change, and deferred spindle service, with runout out of limit on L3-02 and L3-05. Both were introduced with the shift change, so shifts also acted indirectly by removing the service window. Reverting shifts will not confirm or fix anything alone. Do now: pull the Line 6 results, service the spindles, run the Tamsworth trial, add traceability and contain with 100% CMM. Avoid CMM sampling and permanent Corvane adoption.
